Hydroacoustics module. 23 October 2026. Status: literature and held-data review, plus catalogue queries run in code. No hydrophone waveform was processed. All values carry their source in the companion files.

| Catalogues | [hydro-known-sources-catalogue-review.md]({{artifact:7970a3be-d55f-4973-8614-908bdb96b7dc}}) | [source-catalogues.csv]({{artifact:d02397a5-874c-4d63-86bc-8574a9e1e151}}) (45 databases); [known-events-6-10mar2014.csv]({{artifact:df0f8673-f306-41ef-9b41-11e2230e3f70}}) (298 rows) |
| Raw returns | [returned-records-catalogues.zip]({{artifact:a67afdbc-0eaf-42c2-9f2b-99fa59c88386}}); [returned-waveforms-12h.zip]({{artifact:fe96bfde-27f9-40c8-8a61-d211e76deccf}}) (island seismic stations, primary window) | |

## 1. Impact source: what is known

1. **Only one aircraft ocean impact has a peer-reviewed long-range record with ground truth.** It is the F-35A off Misawa, 9 April 2019 (Metz, Obana & Fukao 2023). At H11N and H11S, 3,249-3,341 km away, the arrivals are 6-8 s transients. The onset is emergent and the end is clear. The energy is mostly below 15-25 Hz, with no energy near 20 Hz at any station, near or far. Peak 1-s RMS is 0.31-0.37 Pa (H11N), 12-16 dB above background. The 5-95 % energy span is 3.4-4.8 s. Metz give no energy, source level or coupling.
2. **Metz also give near-field records (180-255 km, cabled seabed stations).** These are the only near-field records of an aircraft ocean impact that were found. The project has not digitised them. They are the best available test of source spectrum and duration with little path distortion.
3. **The 20 Hz spectral gap is in both near and far records.** It is therefore a source or site feature, not a long-path effect (track interpretation).
4. **Kadri 2024 claims of other aircraft are weak evidence.** Six of the eight cases checked are 4-12 min off the water-path time in an exploratory straight-path, one-speed check (registry D13: this is not evidence that Kadri erred), and AF447 and Yemenia 626 have SNR below 2 on Kadri's own figures. No other group has reproduced them. Kadri's energy argument treats kinetic energy as if it were radiated sound.
5. **Swissair 111 (MD-11, 1998, about 2.7 GJ, 55 m water) is a new airliner-energy case.** Land seismographs recorded the impact. No hydroacoustic record was found.
6. **The physics of water entry puts most of the sound in the cavity and bubble phase, not the first slam.** Leslie 1964 (bullets) and Li et al. 2021 (steel balls) agree on this; Kadri's model emphasises the entry phase. Minnaert arithmetic gives 0.5-6.5 Hz resonance for air pockets of 0.5-5 m radius. Airliner-scale cavities may therefore radiate largely below the 4-64 Hz band used for the F-35A, and near the IMS response roll-off. This is provisional.
7. **Implosions of trapped volumes while the wreck sinks are a separate source.** The radiated fraction of P·V is about 18 % for glass spheres and 0.2-0.6 % for ductile metal shells. One deep (more than 1 km) implosion of about 1 m³ could match the F-35A impact in radiated energy. Whether any sealed volume survives an airliner impact is unknown.
8. **Duncan & Dall'Osto 2023 model the MH370 path 20-30 dB weaker than the F-35A path.** Their path is the Curtin 301.6° bearing, not the core region near 37 S.

**Coupling efficiency.** Published and project values span 10⁻¹⁰ to 1. Most of that spread comes from different definitions, not from physics. The track sorted every value into four definition classes:

- D1: inverted through the project's propagation model at a stated source depth.
- D2: Arons-equivalent yield in the sound channel, path-blind.
- D3: measured near the source.
- D4: in one frequency band.

## 1. Open IMS hydrophone background for March (2015-2019 as a stand-in for 2014)

Note: [ims-open-march-background-note.md]({{artifact:e9733f9c-2599-488e-b0ae-29ceff0d1564}}). Tables: [ims-march-false-alarm-rates.csv]({{artifact:da30fe9e-42df-4120-a725-af8b348d18fd}}), [ims-march-noise-percentiles.csv]({{artifact:5934eb83-a597-4e84-b6e2-68eb0b60e8b2}}), [ims-march-noise-vs-references.csv]({{artifact:59ff8cbc-7e16-452a-9072-65ea9adc2d5f}}), [ims-open-availability.csv]({{artifact:648befdb-52d8-49c7-8e23-00b209984bf2}}), [h01w-array-calibration.json]({{artifact:076cefbe-3cb6-4831-8495-2149f256d05a}}).

- **Data used.** EarthScope serves IMS hydrophone data openly from 2015, not for 2014, and none for H08N. The track used the 00:00-04:00 UTC block of every open March day: 115 station-days at H01W and 153 at H08S, 2015-2019. The sandbox link speed (about 1.1 MB/s) forced this cut.
- **Noise (5-40 Hz median in the arrival-window hours).**
  - H01W: 103.6 dB re 1 µPa. That is +2.0 dB above Blackman 2003 and **+7.4 dB above the stand-in the module has used** (registry D06).
  - H08S: 98.0 dB re 1 µPa. That is +2.5 dB above Blackman 2003 and +1.8 dB above the stand-in.
  - **Consequence:** detection estimates at H01W built on the stand-in are optimistic by about 7 dB.
  - **Corroboration from 2014:** the H01W levels digitised earlier from Royer's 2014 spectrogram (about 101.7 dB) and from Kadri's Fig. 9 trace (103.1 dB) agree with the proxy to within about 2 dB. The stand-in, which is the IMOS 3376 5-40 Hz level of 96.2 dB, is therefore the outlier.
- **H01W bearing bias.** Bearings computed from the published element positions are biased by a median of +5.2°, and by up to +12° inside the arc sector. An array calibration on 41 catalogue earthquakes corrects this: left-out error -0.04°, robust standard deviation 0.66°. Any project bearing at H01W computed from element positions needs this check.
- **False-alarm background.** The rate counts coherent arrivals from the 7th-arc sector (20-40 S) in the 2014 clock-time windows that pass the registered 5-40 Hz detector, per hour, with day-bootstrap 90 % intervals.

  | | screen (p < 0.3) | mark (p < 0.1) | report (p < 0.05) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | H01W | 0.139 (0.086-0.194) | 0.125 | 0.086 |
  | H08S | 1.00 (0.72-1.32) | 0.43 | 0.36 |

  The p floors are 1/27,850 (H01W) and 1/39,173 (H08S). The expected count in one arrival window at the screen level is about 0.27 at H01W and about 2.1 at H08S.
  - At H08S, 298 of the 316 arc-direction passes come from 148-163.5°. That is the 35-40 S part of the arc, which is also the direction of Antarctic ice and the ridge to the south. Bearing alone cannot separate an impact there from those sources.
- **8 March 2014 was worse than a typical proxy day at H08S.** In the proxy years, airgun trains fill 30 % or more of the window on 49 of 153 days, all from 108-114°. The 35° train seen on 8 March 2014 never appears.
- **Declared limits:**
  - The class rules were tuned on the 8 March full days.

# F-35A coupling ridge re-derived from the raw Wake Island records (H11N1-3, H11S1-3)

Hydroacoustics module, track 1, 25 Oct 2026. **EXPLORATORY** calibration of the source model on another event (F-35A, 9 Apr 2019). Nothing here returns to end of flight; no received duration is used for MH370. The measurements, the 20 Hz gap test and the ridge were **pre-registered** before computation ([f35a-raw-prereg.md]({{artifact:493a290e-9620-430a-85fe-b6f0ae751a8d}})); the corner-frequency family (Ffit_c), the per-triad RAM delta used as a sensitivity row and the pre-event-only noise σ are **post hoc** and labelled. No detection statistic or p-value is computed here.

## 1. Main findings

1. **The raw records reproduce the digitised Metz numbers.** Exposure 4-64 Hz is +0.22 to +0.29 dB higher than digitised at every element (triads H11N 0.284 vs 0.270 Pa² s, H11S 0.0955 vs 0.0896 Pa² s); 1-s RMS peaks +0.44 to +0.76 dB; noise +0.13 to +0.17 dB; −6 dB widths 0.05-0.30 s shorter; 5-95 % spans 0.08-0.27 s shorter; peak times within ±0.24 s. The N/S exposure split stays at 4.7 dB.
2. **The ~20 Hz gap is real in the raw data at all six elements** (pre-registered G1: "present" at 6/6). Excess-energy notch 18-24 Hz is −7.2 to −12.0 dB (95 % upper bounds −4.99 to −9.43 dB). It is not the instrument (response feature +0.10 dB, smooth through 12-34 Hz), not a noise peak (the noise has a slight dip, −0.2 to −1.7 dB, not a 20 Hz fin-whale-type peak), not noise subtraction (the arrival PSD itself drops 5.0-7.3 dB before subtraction), not Metz filtering (our own processing), and not the modelled TL (KRAKEN TL is smooth through 16-25 Hz). No 60 Hz notch is resolved (2 elements "absent", 4 "unresolved"); the 25-ms two-pulse explanation is therefore not supported where the data have power, but the 60 Hz SNR is low (window/noise 1-2 dB). The received shape matches the digitised shape: received ESD slope 5-40 Hz −4.48 to −5.10 dB/octave (digitised −4.4/−4.8).
3. **Implied source slope agrees with the digitised result; the raw 2-4 Hz bands add a corner.** Source ESD slope 5-40 Hz −10.2 ± 0.7 dB/octave at 10 m (KRAKEN only; digitised far field −10.1 ± 0.5), −9.45 ± 0.8 with RAM, i.e. exponent n ≈ 3.1-3.4. The pre-registered cavity branch is **not supported**: at 2-4 Hz the implied source lies 0 to −10 dB *below* the power-law extrapolation, not ≥3 dB above it. A post hoc fit puts a corner at 4.5-5.75 Hz (1σ 3.5-6.25 Hz) with n 2.65-3.5 above it.
4. **The ridge (D1).** f⁻², KRAKEN+RAM (module convention), 900 MJ: 0.229 / 0.0572 / 0.00925 / 0.00240 / 6.84e-4 / 3.64e-4 / 1.86e-4 at 1/2/5/10/20/30/50 m, 1.06-1.07 × the digitised CV01-CV03. With the data-supported corner (Ffit_c) η is 0.6-1.0 × the f⁻² value at every depth on KRAKEN+RAM. The f⁻⁴ and fitted-no-corner families give 37-61 × and 3-13 × the f⁻² value because they put most energy below 4 Hz, where the raw data show none; they exceed η = 1 (energy limit) at z_eff ≤ 2 m (f⁻⁴) and 1 m (fitted, no corner). Across families η falls by about 1,200-6,400 × from 1 m to 50 m.
5. **The 68 % error budget is dominated by station spread and location**, σ_ln ≈ 0.61 in total (factor 1.84): energy ±200 MJ σ_ln 0.23, element 0.13, station 0.38-0.45, location (module point W vs Metz-consistent point P, 21.4 km apart) 0.30-0.41. The location term is larger than the project's earlier ±8 km test (≤8 %) because P is farther away and on a different TL path.
6. **A new pyram run (per triad) removes most of the H11N/H11S split (gap G-F2).** The module applied the H11S RAM delta to both triads. The H11N delta is smaller at 10-40 Hz (0.36-1.91 dB vs 2.83-3.90 dB at H11S). With each triad's own delta, η_N/η_S at 10 m falls from 2.16 to 1.26 (σ_ln station 0.39 → 0.11) and pooled η at 10 m becomes 1.81e-3 (0.75-0.78 × the module-convention value). The new H11S delta reproduces the module delta to within 0.7 dB.
7. **Near field.** The digitised near-field values are 3.95-4.0 × the raw KRAKEN-only far field and 1.85-1.86 × the raw KRAKEN+RAM far field (previously 4.2 × and ~2.0 ×).
8. **Brown's D2 recomputed.** Raw instantaneous peaks are 0.69-1.29 Pa (4-40 / 4-64 Hz) and 0.93-1.28 Pa (2-100 Hz). Arons D2 (900 MJ) = 5.4e-4 geometric mean in 4-64 Hz (element range 2.9e-4 to 1.0e-3), 4.6e-4 in 4-40 Hz, 7.6e-4 in 2-100 Hz, 2.1e-5 from the 1-s RMS peak. Brown's 0.7 Pa (band not stated) equals our lowest element peak (H11S3, 4-40 Hz, 0.689 Pa) and gives 2.08e-4, 2.2-2.6 × below our geometric means.
9. **Back-azimuth disagrees with Metz by 3-4°.** Plane-wave fits with the FDSN element coordinates give 323.7° (H11N) and 325.7° (H11S), SD ≤ 0.03°, apparent velocity 1452-1456 m/s; the geodesic from W is 320.8° / 322.3° and Metz give 320.6° / 321.7°, 1473 / 1463 m/s. The back-azimuth is not used in the coupling ridge.

## 2. Method (as pre-registered unless stated)

Raw IM.H11N1-3/H11S1-3 EDH, 250 Hz, EarthScope FDSN dataselect (anonymous): event window 10:30-11:40 UTC plus seven 30-min backgrounds (01, 04, 07, 14, 17, 20, 23 h UTC) the same day; StationXML response for 9 Apr 2019 (one channel epoch, 2007-open; coordinates identical to module data/stations.csv). Full response removed to Pa (pre-filt 0.5/1/110/120 Hz). Envelope: 4-pole zero-phase 4-64 Hz, 1-s boxcar mean square, 0.02-s step; module observation operator obs.py unchanged (Metz frames H11N 11:02:55-11:03:25, H11S 11:03:55-11:04:25; noise = median outside peak ±8 s; arrival window L > L_n + 1 dB). Third-octave bands 2-100 Hz over the arrival window ±2 s, noise 10:45-11:01 UTC; a band is "measured" if excess ≥ 2σ (σ from all background windows) and window/noise ≥ 3 dB. TL: module KRAKEN chain unchanged (tl_grid_run_j.run_path + step2_tl loaders; GEBCO_2026, WOA23 B5C2 April, hard bottom, Francois-Garrison), extended to depths 1-50 m and bands 2-100 Hz; it reproduces module step2_tl.csv to < 1e-6 dB on the shared grid. D1 = SE_obs / [E ρc/2π Σ W_b S_b 10^(−TL_b/10)], bands 5-63 Hz, W63 0.54, τ 3.30 s, geometric mean of triads (step2_invert.py relation). D4 = route-B in-band energy / E. D2 = Arons (P = 52.4e6 (R/W^1/3)^−1.13 Pa, R 3248.8 / 3341.5 km, 4.184 MJ/kg).

# Transair 810 (B737-200 ditching off Oahu, 2 July 2021) at Wake Island: first ditching-family (R3) case

Hydroacoustics module, track 2. 25 Oct 2026. Raw IMS records, EarthScope FDSN (net IM, cha EDH, 250 Hz).
Pre-registration written and saved before any statistic was computed on the hydrophone data:
[transair810-preregistration.md]({{artifact:986504a4-4ccc-4c75-82d1-144325a8a08c}}) (SHA-256 360cf299…).
Everything marked EXPLORATORY was added after the first run.

## Summary

1. **NTSB facts (DCA21FA174).** Water impact was at 11:45:17 UTC, at 21.27616 N, 158.02565 W. Groundspeed was 114.6 kt (58.96 m/s), descent rate about 4–6 m/s, pitch +12.3°, bank −14.9°, mass 42.0 t. Kinetic energy is **73.6 MJ (90 % 69.4–77.9)** and vertical kinetic energy 0.56 MJ (0.33–0.85). The project's ~86 MJ was an assumption and is 17 % high. The fuselage broke in two at BS 540. The wreck lies at 104–111 m depth.
2. **Path.** The paths to H11N (3,655 km) and H11S (3,700 km) are clear in deep water: the minimum depth beyond 30 km is 1,329 m, and there is no land on the ±2 km corridor. The only obstacle is the Oahu shelf at the source. Water stays under 200 m for the first 9 km, and the module KRAKEN chain finds no propagating modes at ≤ 40 Hz on the great circle from the NTSB point.
3. **Predicted window (ditching site).** Arrivals are predicted at 12:26:24 UTC (H11N) and 12:26:53 UTC (H11S), with 1σ ≈ 10 s. Neither triad gives a matched-filter p below 0.05: H11N p = 0.079 (mark), H11S p = 0.095 (mark), with n = 1,244 / 1,246 and p floor 0.0008. The bearings at the coherence maxima are 35° and 94° off the expected direction. **No significant detection with limited power.**
4. **Kadri's box.** A signal is present at his time and roughly his level. It does not come from the ditching site.
   - Matched filter: p = 0.0088 at H11N (report) and 0.057 at H11S. At H11S, D1 and coherence are also at mark level.
   - Bearing at H11S: two coherent pulses 42 s apart (12:31:42 and 12:32:24) from **152.6°**, apparent speed 1.44 km/s. The expected bearing is 79.2°.
   - Inter-triad timing: H11N receives both pulses 72–73 s after H11S. A plane wave from 152.6° predicts +74.5 s; a source at the ditching site predicts −29.7 s.
   - Time of flight from 11:45:17 would be 1.30–1.32 km/s, not a deep-channel speed.
   - The source is unidentified and EXPLORATORY: the bearing points toward the Tonga–Kermadec arc, and no USGS (M ≥ 3) or ISC event fits.
5. **Coupling, measured detection probability.** Injecting the real F-35A arrival into 14 days of H11 background gives a 50 % detection level (M1b p < 0.05) of 0.065 Pa (H11N) and 0.048 Pa (H11S), as 1-s RMS in 5–40 Hz.
6. **Coupling upper limit (R3).** Through the module chain (KRAKEN + RAM, source 3 km seaward, f⁻², total KE), η_rad,UL50 at H11S is 3.2e-4 / 1.2e-3 / 7.4e-3 / 3.0e-2 / 0.12 for z_eff = 10 / 5 / 2 / 1 / 0.5 m. H11N is 2.3× looser.
   - This is **0.14× (H11S) and 0.31–0.32× (H11N) the F-35A ridge at the same depth**, measured at 2–10 m and on the extended ridge below 2 m.
   - It is 30–30,000× above the slow-blunt analogs (raindrops ~1e-5, ice blocks ~8e-7). The data therefore exclude an F-35A-like coupling for the ditching but cannot test a slow-blunt one.

Standing caveats on every limit and ratio here:
- (C1) The propagation model failed the frequency-slope check against the 2001 airguns (+10 dB/octave at H01W, +7 at H08S) although levels passed. This work does not test or change that. The upper limit weights 5–63 Hz through the same model, so an unresolved slope error passes into it, unquantified.
- (C2) The detection probability is measured on real background but with a borrowed arrival shape (the F-35A). A longer ditching arrival would make the matched filter less efficient, which would make the limits optimistic.

## 1. Primary facts (NTSB) and kinetic energy

Sources: the NTSB docket at data.ntsb.gov, read in this session. They are the final report (CAROL, 45 pp.), the Aircraft Performance Group (APG) study with Table 4, the FDR specialist's report and its data attachment (CSV), the EGPWS specialist's report, the Search and Recovery factual, the Structures factual and the Survival factual. Second sources are Wikipedia, Aviation Safety Network, Kadri S1 and GEBCO 2026. Table: [ntsb_primary_facts.csv]({{artifact:96e05656-1298-4a2a-932b-4ebeb0a17608}}).

Verifier: T1 T2 AGREE. Erratum 7 applies. (41 files)

# Replication of Kadri (2024) aircraft-crash panels on raw IMS data, and reconciliation (track 4)

Hydroacoustics module, 25 Oct 2026. Pre-registered windows and statistics: {{artifact:0e9cad65-8030-4b8a-8f04-6528e5abbbfd}} (saved before any waveform was downloaded).
Parts marked EXPLORATORY or POST-HOC were not pre-registered. No MH370 quantity is inferred from anything here. No coupling value is derived in this track (no energy or transmission-loss inversion), so no `db_coupling_value.csv` rows are written.

## Deviations and limits (read first)
1. **Citation.** The paper is *Sci. Rep.* **14:10102** (2024), doi 10.1038/s41598-024-60529-1 (not 14:10178; checked in the repo text and PMC copy).
2. **AirAsia 8501, H01W:** open EarthScope data cover only 2014-12-27 22:00:00 – 2014-12-28 00:00:00 UTC (probes: 204 at 21:00, 00:05, 00:30, 02:00, 06:00, 12:00 on 28 Dec; 200 from 29 Dec). The pre-registered water window (00:02:58–00:06:28) is **not testable**; the last minute of Kadri's panel (00:00–00:01) is missing.
3. **AB Aviation 1103:** no official accident report found; impact time 09:30–09:40 UTC from ASN/press (12:30/12:40 EAT); position from Kadri S1 (not verified).
4. **Transair 810:** ditching position from Wikipedia (NTSB final-report coordinates not read); time 11:45:18 ± 60 s from the NTSB docket (ADS-B end 11:45:17.902; 'about 0145 HST').
5. **F-35A:** impact time 10:26:30 UTC from Kadri S1 / JASDF and position from the module working point (Metz 2023); not re-verified (track 1 owns F-35A).
6. **Processing deviation (declared):** the pre-registered 5 % cosine taper (and obspy's default 5 % response-removal taper) damped up to 6 min at the end of the 2-h H01W record and 18 min at the ends of 6-h records; both were capped at 30 s and the edge exclusion widened from 20 s to 60 s; 1-sample chunk-join holes are interpolated instead of zero-filled (zero fill made spikes). Results after the fix differ from the first run by ≤ 0.04 in p except QZ8501 H01W Kadri box (p 0.109 → 0.047, because the box lay inside the damped end).
7. **D1 STA/LTA** is computed on the triad-mean energy (module definition STA 2 s / LTA 30 s otherwise unchanged). **M1b matched filter not run** (its template bank is built for the MH370 ranges; not adapted). **Likelihood ratios not defined** (no calibrated per-case signal model).
8. **Reproduction figure** uses the single element with the highest zero-lag envelope correlation (display choice, not pre-registered).
9. **Bearings at H08S (SJ182, Jan 2021):** elements H08S1/H08S2 are 15–20 dB noisier than H08S3 at 2–20 Hz; triad bearing unreliable. AB1103 box: element delays incoherent; no bearing.
10. **Kadri's panel boxes, traces and levels** are digitised from the publisher's full-resolution PNGs (≈0.78 s/px; trace clipped at the frame). Kadri's Lion Air 904, Yemenia, AF447, Asiana panels are pre-2015 (no open data) and not in scope.
11. Three script artifacts (cases.py, geometry.py, water_route.py) were saved as version 2 of existing same-name project artifacts (likely another track's); earlier versions are retained.

## 1. What Kadri reports (quoted)
Methods: "a high pass Butterworth IIR filter was used (in addition to the CTBTO high pass filter) below 5 Hz. Moreover, a 2–40 [Hz] band-pass filter was applied in general." Panels: "Signals from past aircraft crashes were presented around the middle of a 10 min time window". S1 speed range (MH370 section): "an average speed between 1,450 m/s and 1,570 m/s".
For the crash panels Kadri gives **no numeric signal time, amplitude or bearing**; the claim is the box in each figure. Per case (full quotes in {{artifact:41d9a266-fbed-4cb9-ac7e-4f8e9bd84c42}}, column `kadri_claim`):
* **F-35A** (Fig. 4a; H11N after 10:58, H11S after 10:59): "a distinctive, sharp, and rapid (6 s) signal following the supersonic impact"; S1 impact "10:26:30 UTC", "about 3, 340 km".
* **Sriwijaya 182** (Fig. 4c; H08S after 08:06): "the signal of interest is sharp and clear"; S1 "07:40 UTC", range "4, 694 km" — Fig. 2 map gives "3,772 km, 89.32°".
* **Transair 810** (Fig. 5b; H11N after 12:28, H11S after 12:27): "there appears to be a double signal, potentially indicating a ditching event, an engine that was detached, or signal arrival from different locations"; S1 "around 11:46 UTC".
* **AB Aviation 1103** (Fig. 6a; H08S after 09:36): Fig. 6 "signal dispersion is most pronounced"; S1 "around 09:30 UTC"; Fig. 2 "3,186 km, 258.47°".
* **AirAsia 8501** (Fig. 6b; H01W only, after 23:51): "distorted with noise (possibly due to airgun shots ...), and the magnitude of the pressure induced by the aircraft crash is not clear"; S1 "December 28, 2014 ... around 07:37 UTC"; Fig. 2 "3,523 km, 351.52°".
Digitised box limits (min after panel start): F-35A H11N 4.26–5.69, H11S 4.38–5.81; SJ182 4.58–6.01; TA810 H11N 4.24–5.68, H11S 4.20–5.65; AB1103 4.62–6.09; QZ8501 4.10–5.73 ({{artifact:ef2da099-bf3b-4d6f-9b5d-ebcc9bbb3a6f}}); agree with the project's earlier 669-px reads within 0.06 min.

## 2. Impact times and positions (primary sources) vs Kadri
* QZ8501: KNKT final report "The last data recorded by FDR was at 2320:35 UTC" (27 Dec), radio altitude 118 ft. The project table's "2014-12-28 ~07:37" (from Kadri S1) is **not supported**; Kadri's own panel (23:51) implies he used a ~23:2x time. Kadri's S1 position is 286.6 km from the KNKT site; his Fig. 2 range (3,523 km) is close to our KNKT-site range (3,492.1 km).

Rep. 14:10102) is a COMPARISON SET: F-35A reproduced and consistent; Transair, Sriwijaya, AB1103, AirAsia boxed signals real but not consistent with the crash sites under the project path model; Lion Air 610 no detection. Not evidence that Kadri erred. Verifier: K2 K3 AGREE, K1 MINOR. Errata 2 and 3 apply. (16 files)

# Absolute level check of the propagation chain on known-energy explosions, and the ARA San Juan event, from raw IMS data

Hydroacoustics module, track 3, 25 October 2026. Exploratory, with a protocol written before any statistic was computed
(section 1; timestamp 2026-10-25T01:45:53Z). Nothing here is a likelihood and nothing moves the posterior. Standing caveats:
(1) frequency-slope failure of the propagation model on the 2001 airguns (+10 dB/oct H01W, +7 dB/oct H08S) — section 5 says how
this result changes it; (2) detection probability is a proxy unless measured on real data — section 6 gives the first real-data
measurement for M1b. Units: Pa, Pa^2 s, dB re 1 uPa (peak), dB re 1 uPa^2 s/Hz (band-average energy spectral density, ESD).

## Results in one paragraph
Raw IMS records at Ascension (H10N, H10S; EarthScope, anonymous) were downloaded for the San Juan calibration charge, the San Juan
loss event and all eight US Navy shock-trial shots (2016 x 5, 2021 x 3). The raw data reproduce the published levels: San Juan
peaks at H10N 138.2 dB re 1 uPa (Vergoz: 139), charge 128.5 dB (Vergoz: 130); the digitised Nielsen Fig. 5c PSD is matched by a
raw 60 s Welch PSD within 1.7 dB. **The stage-1b level FAIL (-14.4 dB) was mostly a unit conversion.** The digitised PSD was
converted to energy with a 10 s signal duration; the raw data show that the averaging window was about 50 s (39-71 s by band),
so that step understated the measured energy by about 7 dB. On raw data the charge at H10N is -2.8 to -8.2 dB (model too loud,
spread set by the source model), and at H10S it is -0.9 to +5.7 dB. Across 17 explosion-station pairs, 2 chains and 3 declared
source models, **the residual frequency slope is -3.7 to +2.9 dB/octave; none shows the airgun-type +7 to +13 dB/octave.**
Absolute level scatters by about 4-5 dB (SD over pairs, KRAKEN-only) about a bias that depends on the source model and, for the
shock trials, on a charge depth that no primary source gives. The model does not reproduce the H10S-H10N station difference for
the South American sources (measured +5.4 dB, predicted -1 to -2 dB), consistent with unmodelled Rio Grande Rise blockage on
the H10N path. The module's M1b matched filter detects the real San Juan arrival at p = 0.0026 (the floor, n = 379) at all five
usable elements, and the charge at p = 0.0027-0.0082; but background windows reach 0.93-0.98 on the same statistic. Through the
same chain the San Juan event is a 9-918 kg TNT-equivalent source for depths 200-900 m (G&S construction and 800 ft reference; up to 2,059 kg with the 300 ft reference; Heyburn et al. 2020: 428 kg lies inside
the range only for depths of about 800-900 m).

## 1. Pre-registration (written before computing; full text `prereg.md`)
Disclosure: the charge result at H10N was not blind (stage 1b digitised result known). Raw measurements, H10S, the FSST shots,
the second source model and the San Juan event were blind. Measurement (M1-M8): full StationXML response removed (input unit
PA, checked); arrival = 1-s RMS envelope peak (2-40 Hz) in [d/1.500 - 60 s, d/1.460 + 60 s]; signal window 60 s centred on the peak
(20 s and 120 s sensitivity); noise = median of 10 equal windows ending 60 s before; FFT ESD in base-2 third octaves, noise

Verifier: P1 P3 AGREE, P2 MINOR. Errata 5 and 6 apply. (57 files)

"""Merge the wave-3 DB rows from three tracks into one import set with unique ids.

Each track numbered its new rows from CV26 / OB07, so the ids collide. This script
gives every row a unique id that follows the base package (CV01-CV25, OB01-OB06),
keeps the track's own id in column `track_local_id`, and remaps id references in
db_impact_case_AC05_update.csv. Values are not changed.
Order: propagation check (keeps CV26-CV31, OB07-OB63), then Transair 810, then F-35A raw ridge.
"""
import re, sys
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

root = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
pkg = Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
out = root / "db-rows-merged"

cv_src = [("propagation-level-check", "propagation-level-check/db_coupling_value_new_rows.csv"),
          ("transair-810", "transair-810/db_coupling_value_new_rows.csv"),
          ("f35a-raw-ridge", "f35a-raw-ridge/f35a-raw-coupling-rows.csv")]
ob_src = [("propagation-level-check", "propagation-level-check/db_received_observation.csv"),
